description: TigerShark Science develops human skin models from stem cells, replicating structures like hair and nerves, to provide realistic alternatives to animal testing.

universities: Fraunhofer Institute for Silicate Research ISC
prior_companies: Fraunhofer Institute for Silicate Research ISC
founders_enriched.source_of_identity: Biologist and project manager at the Translational Center for Regenerative Therapies (TLC-RT) of the Fraunhofer Institute for Silicate Research ISC.

funding_summary: In 2024, TigerShark Science received €1.3 million in EXIST funding.
inflection_why_now: The increasing ethical and regulatory pressures against animal testing in the pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries create a timely demand for advanced in-vitro models.
devils_advocate_risks: Scalability: Challenges in mass-producing complex skin models could hinder widespread adoption.
Regulatory Acceptance: Gaining regulatory approval for new testing methods may be time-consuming and uncertain.

lp_synergy_matches.reason: As a pharmaceutical company, Boehringer Ingelheim could benefit from TigerShark Science's advanced in-vitro skin models for drug testing.
Evonik's focus on specialty chemicals aligns with TigerShark Science's development of complex skin models, potentially enhancing material science applications.
